title: Comprehensive accessibility sweep: tokens, interactive components, and VPAT alignment
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Scope: Run a component-level accessibility audit across the design system focusing on tokens (color/typography), interactive controls (buttons, icon buttons, dropdowns), tables (row focus/headers/ARIA), and data visualizations (charts and legends). The goal is to remediate issues that block a VPAT update and produce developer-ready guidance and a set of PRs for engineering.

Deliverables: 1) Audit report with prioritized findings and remediation plan; 2) Token adjustments and contrast relabeling PRs; 3) Component patches for ARIA attributes and keyboard navigation; 4) Updated VPAT draft and confluence artifact linking to implementation PRs; 5) QA checklist for future regressions.

Scope notes/constraints: We will not redesign component interactions (e.g., change multi-select UX) unless required for conformance. Design to provide CSS and token-proposal artifacts; Engineering to own implementation PRs and e2e keyboard/contrast tests. Work will be coordinated with Platform/Eng to schedule any runtime changes to focus rings and focus management in hosted components.
acceptance_criteria: All identified WCAG 2.1 AA issues in the audit have either an implementation PR or an accepted exception documented in VPAT.
Contrast token map updated and QA'd; automated contrast check added to token CI job or documented mitigation.
Buttons and interactive controls have visible focus states, correct ARIA roles, and keyboard order verified in cross-browser testing.
Tables: header associations (th/scope or aria-labelledby), row focus/selection patterns, and screen-reader reading order validated.
Charts: accessible descriptions (aria-describedby/role=img with fallback text), keyboard focus for interactive chart elements, and colorblind-friendly palette tokens applied where applicable.
VPAT draft updated and linked to specific PRs and test artifacts in Confluence; legal/ops review scheduled.
notes: Design decision: prefer token-level contrast fixes over per-component overrides so downstream consumers inherit accessible defaults.
Trade-off: slightly heavier focus rings on primary buttons to meet contrast on dark backgrounds; will coordinate with brand team for approval.
Edge case: legacy table markup used by onboarding flow will require a small wrapper that adds aria attributes; ENG estimate required (see dependencies).
